episodes.191720: A strong upper level high pressure remained over southern California and Nevada with higher moisture across central and eastern NM. Strong daytime heating resulted in the development of showers and storms across the higher terrain of central New Mexico around midday July 9th with storms slowly drifting to the southeast. Storms over the Sacramento Mountains dropped 1 to 2 inches of rain on the South Fork and Salt Fire burn scars around Ruidoso. This resulted in catastrophic burn scar flash flooding and debris flows in the Rio Ruidoso, NM48, and U.S. Highway 70 from Alto east to Ruidoso Downs. The runoff and debris flow caused the Rio Ruidoso at Hollywood to quickly spike to 11.65 feet in the mid afternoon. A landspout was also observed in the upper canyon area west of downtown Ruidoso. Neighborhoods west of downtown Ruidoso were evacuated and 64 swift water rescues were conducted. Storms exited east of Ruidoso late in the afternoon with flash flooding subsiding in the evening. Elsewhere in the state, isolated severe storms produced quarter size hail at Chamizal in Socorro County and a mile east of Ute Park in Colfax County. Storms across central and eastern New Mexico dissipated overnight. Another round of storms developed across the central mountain chain midday July 10th. Multiple rounds of training storms over the Sacramento Mountains dropped a half inch to two inches across the Ruidoso area including the South Fork and Salt Fire burn scars. This resulted in a second consecutive day of catastrophic flash flooding, debris flows and road collapses in the same areas of Ruidoso. Several swift water rescues were conducted again along U.S. Highway 70. The Rio Ruidoso at Hollywood spiked to a record level of 12.51 feet from the runoff and debris flow off the burn scars. Storms and high flows in area creeks and streams across Ruidoso slowly decreased during the evening hours. Elsewhere, storms caused high wind gusts at the Little Burro mesonet on the White Sand Missile Range and at the Dunken Mesonet on the White Sands Missile Range. Storms across the state dissipated shortly after sunset. Another round of diurnal storms developed during the afternoon and evening hours on July 11th. Outflow winds from thunderstorms resulted in roof damage to a residence in Little Water in west central San Juan County.
episodes.191832: After a break in monsoon storm activity, widespread shower and thunderstorm activity impacted much of southeast Arizona. The main impacts were strong gusty winds and areas of blowing dust.
episodes.191855: In the evening hours of July 11th, storms brought hail to portions of Henry County and then Platte County, MO.
episodes.191945: A very strong mid level ridge slowly moved through the region, resulting in multiple days of excessive heat. At least one instance of injury and fatality were reported from the heat. The strong ridge eventually shifted far enough east and south of the area to allow sufficient moisture to return, resulting in the development of diurnal convection, with some thunderstorms yielding strong wind gusts.
episodes.192285: An isolated thunderstorm produced a brief non-supercell tornado in rural northeastern Washington county.
episodes.192331: Deep inverted-V soundings, combined with limited yet sufficient moisture to result in a few thunderstorms across the region July 11. The strongest storm, which moved through Judith Gap, produced a severe caliber wind gust.
episodes.192437: A thunderstorm produced localized gale-force winds over the Tangier Sound.
episodes.193385: A stalled frontal boundary over eastern sections of North Carolina retrograded westward during the afternoon and evening as a surface low formed along the front. Ongoing showers and storms become more numerous in the late morning and into the early evening hours. Heavy embedded storms were particularly prevalent across Wake and Orange Counties, leading to isolated flash flooding.
episodes.193455: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over northern Harding County, producing large hail northwest of Ludlow.
episodes.193526: Scattered thunderstorms moved across east-central Kansas during the early morning hours on both July 12 and 13, producing isolated hail, gusty winds, and flooding.
episodes.193714: During the evening hours, a line of thunderstorms developed over Northeast Colorado and the Nebraska Panhandle and moved southeast. An embedded storm developed along the Colorado/Nebraska state line where it moved over the town of Haigler and produced the lone severe thunderstorm wind gust of 58 mph.
episodes.193790: A weak mid-level low over the Florida Peninsula and increasing atmospheric moisture supported the development of numerous slow-moving showers and thunderstorms on the afternoon and evening of July 11th across South Florida.
episodes.194300: Under northeasterly flow due to high pressure situated near southern Nevada, thunderstorm activity, fueled by 500-1000 J/KG of MLCAPE, developed along the Mogollon Rim and White Mountains and moved southwestward towards Gila County and most of southeastern AZ. Activity weakened before reaching the south-central AZ lower deserts due to strong convective inhibition. DCAPE values, however, were near 2000 J/KG across the lower deserts of south-central AZ and thus conditions were favorable for long traveling deep outflow boundaries. One such outflow boundary emanating from higher terrain activity affected the Phoenix area, with the strongest winds observed across the Phoenix East Valley where gusts upwards of 50 mph were observed.
episodes.194386: Thunderstorms developed during the late-afternoon to evening hours in Southern Illinois. These storms were generally sub-severe but one particularly strong storm produced widespread tree and powerline damage in Sesser and Benton in Franklin County. MLCAPE was 1000-1500 J/kg while effective bulk shear was low.
episodes.194387: Isolated thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours on the 12th in the Quad State. Wind damage occurred in the town of Sesser, including tree and powerline damage. Storms from the previous evening in Sesser might have made some trees more susceptible to damage. Meanwhile, torrential rainfall with nearly stationary storms near Tamaroa produced flash flooding. Isolated storms continued overnight as heavy rain and minimal storm motion caused flash flooding issues in Murphysboro and other locations in or near Jackson County, Illinois. Storm total rainfall peaked around 2-3 inches in parts of Jackson and Perry Counties, most of which fell within an hour or two at each respective location. Shear was minimal while SBCAPE reached 2000-3000 J/kg during the afternoon on the 12th, dropping to 1000-2000 J/kg overnight. PW values were near 1.75 inch.
episodes.194471: Conditions became favorable for waterspouts in the afternoon hours as showers and thunderstorms developed just off the southeast South Carolina coast. With plentiful low-level moisture and weak surface winds, a waterspout developed just off the coast of Isle of Palms.
episodes.194570: An isolated severe storm developed over northern Butler County during the afternoon of July 11 and produced up to two inch hail just north of El Dorado. Another cluster of strong to severe storms managed to produce ping pong ball sized hail later that night in Allen County.
episodes.194642: Thunderstorms developed initially over western North Dakota during the afternoon and early evening hours before also forming over central North Dakota later in the evening. This as an upper level short wave trough approached the area and a frontal boundary moved in from Montana. The first storm to develop was over Dunn County and quickly produced a tornado. The tornado occurred over an open field south of Manning and impacted no structures. There was no damage to evaluate, therefore it was rated EF-U (Unknown) by NWS policy. Thereafter, the main threat with the thunderstorms was large hail. The largest reported hail was the size of a baseball, and also occurred in Dunn County. There were also reports of severe wind gusts, particularly towards the end of the event with the later storms. With that said, the strongest wind gust did occur during the middle of the event near Plaza, Mountrail County, where estimated 75 mph wind gusts cause tree damage.
episodes.194674: Scattered thunderstorms along a frontal boundary produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of central and eastern Virginia.
episodes.194675: Scattered thunderstorms along a frontal boundary produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of the Lower Maryland Eastern Shore.
episodes.194676: Scattered thunderstorms along a frontal boundary produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of northeast North Carolina.
episodes.194702: Scattered thunderstorms along a frontal boundary produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.194723: Interaction between the afternoon sea breeze and a weak surface trough over the area produce thunderstorms resulting in around 2 inches of rain causing flooding near Tampa in Hillsborough County.
episodes.194725: An isolated severe storm brought down a large tree.  No other severe reports were received.
episodes.194873: Thunderstorm developed under ridge of high pressure and caused strong winds when it weakened and collapsed.
episodes.194960: Monsoon moisture moving in from the south fueled isolated thunderstorms, a few of which produced high winds. In addition, a wildfire of unknown origin damaged infrastructure on the southeast edge of Kingman.
episodes.194989: A severe thunderstorm developed during the late evening hours of July 11, 2024 and affected Benton County with ping pong ball size hail.
episodes.194990: A cluster of thunderstorms developed in an area of uncapped elevated instability over southeast Kansas on July 11, 2024 and moved into southwest Missouri during the early morning of July 12. As a result, heavy rainfall between 4.0 and 7.70 inches fell in Jasper County, causing flash flooding. An estimated 2-3 feet of water was flowing through the ballfields at Landreth Park, with a water rescue performed in Jasper County.
episodes.194995: A cluster of thunderstorms developed in an area of uncapped elevated instability over southeast Kansas during the late hours of July 11, 2024 and continued into the early morning hours of July 12. A severe thunderstorm affected Crawford County with quarter size hail.
episodes.194996: A cluster of thunderstorms developed in an area of uncapped elevated instability over southeast Kansas during the late hours of July 11, 2024 and continued into the early morning of July 12. As a result, heavy rain between 3.25 and 4.89 inches fell over Cherokee County. A severe thunderstorm also produced damaging winds, resulting in trees down in Cherokee County.
episodes.195085: Monsoon moisture continued to increase over northern Arizona with scattered showers and thunderstorms. A few thunderstorms became severe.
episodes.195129: An isolated severe thunderstorm occurred in Camas.
episodes.195175: A few thunderstorms developed along a stalled boundary. One storm produced a lightning strike that caused some damage.
episodes.195220: Enough moisture remained in the atmosphere to fuel a few showers forming on the southern San Juan mountains. These showers and storms eventually drifted southward over southern La Plata county. With very dry surface air in place on this day, these showers and storms were predominantly producing gusty outflow winds and frequent lightning.
